messages:
maria: heads up — i'm prototyping a tiny 'observer' service that watches KV prefix residency across nodes and emits potential soft-gc/eviction candidates. goal: reduce noisy scans in runtime and give ops a read-only view for debugging.

sam: curious — how does this differ from the existing lease/handshake events? will it subscribe to the event stream or poll snapshots?

maria: great q. plan is hybrid: subscribe to the changefeed for deltas + occasional snapshot to rehydrate if we miss events. deltas are used for hotness counters, snapshot for correctness after restarts.

dennis: watch out for semantics during handoff. if you observe a prefix in node A then see a demote event, you might still have stale belief about residency until handshake completes. need clear invariants.

maria: yep — thinking of two invariants in the API: 1) observed view is eventually consistent (may lag) and 2) each candidate includes a 'certainty' enum {confirmed, likely, stale}. runtime publishes the certainty based on handshake state.

neha: sounds useful for ops dashboards. can the observer also query per-prefix metadata like last-write-epoch and last-prefetch-ts? that helps rule out races when deciding soft-gc.

maria: yes — metadata will be included but read-only. trying to avoid adding any control-plane power so we don't introduce another path that changes ownership. observer must never trigger demotes directly.

sam: interface idea: two endpoints  — /snapshot?shard=X (full) and /stream?since=Y (delta). deltas are compacted as arrays of {prefix, op, epoch, seq, certainty}.

postgres-bot: deploy queued by ci: observer/proto v0.1 -> canary on shard-1

dennis: implementation tradeoff: embed observer inside runtime vs sidecar process. embed = perfect read visibility (no RPC), sidecar = safer separation and easier rollout. Which lane?

maria: leaning sidecar so we don't bloat runtime. but we need efficient wire format and backpressure so sidecar doesn't overwhelm runtime on busy shards.

sam: for sidecar, add a lightweight streaming RPC using the same proto as lease events. push-based with client ack windows. keep per-connection flow-control.

neha: operational concerns: metrics for observer-lag, missed-events, and delta-apply-errors. also an endpoint to request a reconciliation snapshot for a given shard/prefix when debugging.

dennis: correctness during prefix transfer: observer must tie deltas to a transfer-epoch id. if transfer aborts and retried, older deltas should be ignored. recommend delta carry (transfer_epoch, seq).

maria: agreed. will include transfer_epoch + seq and a small client-side TTL for entries. also adding a 'handshake_inflight' flag per-prefix to mark when we expect transient staleness.

sam: curious about cost: does streaming all deltas double our network egress? we host a lot of shards. maybe we sample hot prefixes or enable observer per-priority tenant only.

neha: make observer opt-in per-cluster or per-tenant. default off. for canary: enable for 3 internal tenants and one noisy customer sim.

maria: proof-of-concept API sketch (very rough):

```
GET /v1/observer/snapshot?shard=12
200 OK
[
  {"prefix":"t/42/x","residency":"hot","last_prefetch":1710001000,"transfer_epoch":1234,"certainty":"confirmed"},
  {"prefix":"t/17/y","residency":"cold","last_prefetch":1709995000,"transfer_epoch":1232,"certainty":"likely"}
]

// stream endpoint (server-sent events or grpc stream)
stream item = {prefix, op: "residency_update"|"handoff"|"tombstone", epoch, seq, certainty}
```

maria: note: the API intentionally mirrors runtime terminology to avoid mapping bugs.

dennis: also add a compact 'proof' blob for confirmed events: small byte array signed by runtime containing (prefix, epoch, seq) so external tools can verify an event wasn't forged when debugging multi-DC incidents.

neha: security check — observer read-only, but we still need RBAC + auditing for who queried what prefixes (PII tenancy). integrate with current KMS/KV audit logs.

sam: operational playbook item: when observer-lag > 30s, flip runtime sampling to emit checkpoints and force a snapshot. also surface suspected double-ownership alerts to eng-oncall.

maria: spike plan: build sidecar prototype, implement stream + snapshot, add basic metrics and a small UI tab in console. timeframe: 2w spike + 1w canary.

dennis: tests: unit for epoch/seq ordering, integration to simulate aborted handoffs, and a chaos test that drops 10% of deltas.

neha: i'm adding an oncall runbook entry and a short audit checklist.

sam: 👍 can you open an RFC-ish doc for the API + invariants? i can review and we can fold into the ownership RFC.

maria: will do. creating doc + linking canary plan. thanks all. :rocket:
